text: Triggered on push to main with the path filter skills/** , so docs-only or workflow-only merges don't run it. The workflow grants packages: write only to this job and uses the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN — no PAT, no org secret. actions/checkout@v6 with fetch-depth: 0 for the full history. Install uv (SHA-pinned astral-sh/setup-uv ). Re-validate every skill with uv run python scripts/validate_skill.py --all — last line of defence before bytes leave the repo. actions/setup-node@v6 targeting Node 24, with registry-url: https://npm.pkg.github.com and scope: @bcgov . Run .github/scripts/publish-changed-skills.sh , which diffs BEFORE_SHA against HEAD_SHA , walks each changed skill, and runs npm publish with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} . Already-published versions are skipped. A merge that doesn't bump a skill's package.json version is a no-op for that skill — re-publishing is impossible by design. Bumping the version is what ships a release. See Versioning .

GitHub Packages always requires authentication , even for public packages on the npm registry — this is a GitHub Packages behaviour, not a permission setting on this repo. The flow below uses the GitHub CLI to mint a short-lived token, so you don't need to manage a personal access token.

text: The local-dev flow uses gh to mint a short-lived NODE_AUTH_TOKEN for npm. See the official install guide . # Windows (PowerShell) winget install --id GitHub.cli # macOS brew install gh # Linux — see the install guide for your distro Then sign in: gh auth login gh auth status You also need Node.js installed (any LTS works; the publish pipeline uses Node 24).

sectionTitle: Step 1 — Point npm at GitHub Packages
text: Create a project-local .npmrc beside the package.json where you want to consume the skill. The same file works in local dev and GitHub Actions — the only thing that changes is where NODE_AUTH_TOKEN comes from. @bcgov:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} always-auth=true ${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} is expanded by npm at install time from the environment variable; the literal string lives in the file, so it's safe to commit.

sectionTitle: Step 2 — Get a token into NODE_AUTH_TOKEN
text: Choose the path that matches where you're running npm install .

text: First time only — grant your CLI token the read:packages scope: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages When prompted "Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials?", answer No if you already have Git auth working (especially SSH commit signing) — the prompt is unrelated to npm and answering yes can overwrite Git settings. Every shell session, export the CLI's current token as NODE_AUTH_TOKEN : # PowerShell $env:NODE_AUTH_TOKEN = gh auth token # bash / zsh export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) Want to revoke npm access later? gh auth logout ends both your gh session and any NODE_AUTH_TOKEN that came from it — credential management stays in one place.

text: npm error 401 Unauthorized NODE_AUTH_TOKEN is empty or the token doesn't have read:packages . Re-run gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages . Re-export the token in the current shell: $env:NODE_AUTH_TOKEN = gh auth token (PowerShell) or export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) (bash). Confirm echo $env:NODE_AUTH_TOKEN / echo "$NODE_AUTH_TOKEN" prints a non-empty value. npm error 404 Not Found The version doesn't exist, or the registry is wrong. Check: The catalog for the published version. Your .npmrc has @bcgov:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com . You're running npm install from the directory containing that .npmrc . npm picks the wrong registry / falls back to npmjs.org Make sure the scope and the auth line both point at GitHub Packages — they must both be present in .npmrc : @bcgov:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} always-auth=true If you also have a global ~/.npmrc with a different registry= , the scoped registry line wins — but the auth line must match the URL of whatever registry actually serves the install. GitHub Actions: 403 Forbidden when reading the package Your workflow job is missing permissions: packages: read . The default GITHUB_TOKEN permission profile in many orgs only grants contents: read , so npm gets denied. Add the block in the snippet above to the job (not the workflow root — job-scoped permissions override). Can I use a personal access token (PAT) instead of gh auth token ? Yes — a classic PAT with read:packages works in place of the CLI-issued token. The CLI flow is just lower friction (no separate token to generate, rotate, or revoke), and gh auth logout cleans up both your CLI session and any token sourced from it. text: Keep skills focused — one clear purpose per skill. Write descriptions that make it obvious when a skill should fire. Prefer clarity over cleverness; these are shared across many teams. sectionTitle: Why does this repo only host BC Gov–specific skills?
text: Generic skills — Azure SDKs, Microsoft Foundry, M365, document formats, language workflows — are already maintained in larger upstream catalogues ( listed on Contribute ). Duplicating them here would fragment the ecosystem and double the maintenance cost without giving consumers anything they couldn't already get. What's missing upstream is the BC Gov–specific layer: Public Cloud Landing Zone constraints, internal services, policy-driven workflows, organisational conventions. That's the gap this repo fills, and the bar we apply when reviewing new skills.

sectionTitle: Why GitHub Packages and not public npm?
text: Three reasons: Scoped to the org. The @bcgov scope on GitHub Packages lives inside the same GitHub org that owns the repo — same access surface, same audit log, same identity. Public npm would introduce a second account, a second set of tokens to rotate, and a second place secrets can leak. Token-free CI. Workflows in this org can publish and consume with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN . No bot account, no NPM_TOKEN secret to manage. Right audience. These skills encode BC Gov rules — they aren't designed for general public consumption. Hosting them on GitHub Packages signals "made for the org" without forcing the catalog to be private.

sectionTitle: Why does installing a "public" package still need authentication?
text: This is a GitHub Packages behaviour, not a permission on this repo. The npm registry GitHub runs ( npm.pkg.github.com ) requires a token on every install — even for packages anyone can read. There is no anonymous read path. The good news is that the token doesn't have to be sensitive: any GitHub user can mint a short-lived one with gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages , and CI gets one for free via secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN . See Consume → Step 2 .

sectionTitle: Why the GitHub CLI instead of a personal access token?
text: Both work. The CLI flow is just lower friction: One credential to manage (your gh auth login ), not two. Short-lived tokens by default — rotation is automatic when you re-authenticate. gh auth logout cleans up both your CLI session and any NODE_AUTH_TOKEN sourced from it. No "is this PAT still in use anywhere?" graveyard to maintain. If your environment can't run gh (locked-down CI runner, etc.), a classic PAT with read:packages is a drop-in replacement.

sectionTitle: Why can't I open a PR from a fork?
text: The PR workflow has a fork-gate job that fails any PR whose head repo isn't this one. That failure cascades into the results aggregator, which is the required status check on main . The reason: fork PRs would let untrusted code influence what we validate (and, potentially, what we publish). Maintainers re-land fork-style contributions by pushing the change to an in-repo branch after review. If you don't have push access to bcgov/agent-skills , file an issue describing what you'd like to add. See Pipeline → PR workflow for the full rationale.

text: A contributed skill under skills/ ships as a versioned npm package, so it MUST include a package.json beside its SKILL.md . Meta-skills under .github/skills/ are never published, so a package.json is optional there — and validated only when one is present. Field Type Notes name string Scoped package name — @bcgov/skill-<skill-name> . version string Semver ( MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH ). The source of truth for releases. { "name": "@bcgov/skill-example-skill", "version": "0.1.0", "publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com" } } The entire skill directory is bundled automatically. Do not add a files field — that turns npm into a whitelist and would silently drop directories. To exclude scratch files, add a .npmignore inside the skill folder (it must not exclude SKILL.md ). The publish workflow reads name + version from this file and skips any version already published — bumping version is what ships a new release. See Contribute → Versioning for the npm version flow.

text: For each changed skill, the validator confirms all of the following. If you see a failure on a PR, this list maps directly to the checks. The SKILL.md starts with a closed YAML frontmatter block that parses as a mapping. name and description are present and non-empty. name is kebab-case, at most 64 characters, and matches the skill's directory name . description is at most 1024 characters and contains no angle brackets. No unexpected frontmatter keys are present (only name , description , owner , tags , license , allowed-tools , compatibility , metadata ). The body has an H1 title. All seven required sections are present: Use When , Don't Use When , Workflow , Rules , Examples , Edge Cases , References . None of those required sections is empty. The whole SKILL.md is at most 500 lines. Any bundled scripts/ , references/ , or assets/ directory is flat — no nested subdirectories. For a published skill under skills/ , a package.json sits beside the manifest with a valid name and a semver version , and does not pin a files whitelist. For a meta-skill under .github/skills/ , a missing package.json is allowed; if one is present it is held to the same rules.
